stage1.impression: A moody, believable long-room night shot: the haze in the pendant cones, the fir beams and the run of stools give it depth, and the exposure is in the right range. But the hero speaker is a small red smudge about 40 px tall at the vanishing point, half hidden behind stools and the listening-room chairs. The right-hand booths sink into orange-black mud. Up close, the frosted back-bar reads as flat grey fog, the screen reads as a framed print, and the floor carries a repeating chain of hard elliptical stool shadows. That says competent render, not photograph.

blocking_9: The Ember speaker reads as the hero at a glance: its tinted silhouette and the light through its acrylic are legible and not blocked by stools or chairs, at about 4 % of the frame or more
The booths along the right wall hold detail: the tan leather, the fir caps and a table lamp's pool, with region [470,260,720,480] lum_median >= 18 and crush_pct < 15
The shadows are warm but not monochrome orange: the concrete and ceiling read warm grey (b_median of the ceiling >= 14), not rust
The frosted screens glow evenly as backlit panels set flush, not as framed prints on the wall
The back-bar's clear acrylic shelves show polished, glowing edges and clean reflections in place of an even grey veil
The floor shows soft, overlapping pools of light, not a regular chain of hard identical stool-shadow ellipses
Signs of life and no repeated copies: stools at varied angles, a coat, glasses half full, a record out of its sleeve
Delivered at full 2400 x 1600 with no denoiser smear on the beams' grain or the concrete

defects.what: The Ember speaker is tiny and partly hidden behind the far stools. Its red glow is the only colour but too small to read as a product; it reads as a red light or an exit sign
The listening-room lounge chairs are black silhouettes that fill the vanishing point and pull the eye away from the speaker
The booths are crushed: median 7.2, crush 31 %. The leather and fir caps are nearly invisible
The right-hand edge is a dark, empty slab (crush 20.5 %)
The floor shows a regular row of hard, identical elliptical shadow pools from the stools under the pendant spots. It reads as CG, and the polish shows no reflection of the bar's light
The back-bar's acrylic and shelves read as a flat grey veil (haze plus frosting). The bottles are barely legible and no shelf edge glows
The frosted screen reads as a framed print hung on the wall (median 59, flat), not as a backlit frosted panel set into the concrete
Small cyan-blue rectangles on the bar top (menus or devices) are the only cool colour in the frame and read as phone screens
Ten identical stools at identical angles: repeated copies of one model
The ceiling and beams are a uniform rust brown (r 37, g 17, b 10). The fir shows no checks or end grain at this size, and the shadows are monochrome orange

changes.problem: The hero speaker fills under 0.5 % of the frame and the far stools and lounge chairs block it, so it does not read at a glance.

evidence.measured: about 40 x 50 px of a 720 x 480 proof; lum_median 57, clip 1.1 %; stools overlap its left half and the chairs fill [330,230,440,310]

change.to: position [5.5, 2.0, 1.25] (seated height, beside the booths), target [16.5, 3.6, 1.0], 40 mm, focus at the partition about [15.0, 3.4, 1.0], f/4. This keeps the bar run on the left and frames the Ember clear of the stools and chairs

changes.expected: The speaker fills about 4 to 6 % of the frame, reads as a tinted horn cabinet through the smoked partition and sits near the right third. The bar's perspective still leads to it.

changes.problem: The booths along the right wall are crushed to near black, so a third of the frame is empty and the room loses its cozy, lived-in side.

change.setting: EARF Moon: the lamp in each table lamp; candles
change.from: table lamp 120 W; candles 9 x 2.4 W
change.to: table lamp 220 W; candles 4.0 W, with one candle and one lit table lamp on each visible booth table

changes.expected: A warm pool on each booth table that picks out the leather seat and the fir cap above it, with dark between the pools.

changes.problem: The whole frame is graded monochrome rust, so the concrete, steel and fir lose their own colours and the speaker's red does not stand apart.

evidence.measured: ceiling r 37, g 17, b 10; booths r 13, g 6, b 3; the shadows are almost pure orange

change.to: 2600 (nearer the 2400 to 2700 K sources, so the concrete reads warm grey and the steel near black)

changes.expected: Shadows warm but neutral-leaning. The concrete and steel separate from the fir, and the Ember's red is the only saturated hue.

changes.problem: Hard 950 W pendant spots cast a regular chain of crisp, identical stool-shadow ellipses down the floor, which reads as CG.

evidence.measured: lum_range 63.6, with sharp elliptical light and dark bands repeating at regular intervals

change.from: 3 x spot 950 W, cone 40 deg, point source
change.to: 3 x spot 700 W, cone 55 deg, with spot radius / soft size 0.12 m and blend 0.6; floor polish roughness up a little (about 0.35) so it carries a soft smear of the bar's light

changes.expected: Soft, overlapping pools with blurred shadow edges, and a faint warm reflection of the bar top on the concrete floor.

changes.problem: The frosted screen in the concrete reads as a framed print, not a glowing frosted panel.

evidence.measured: lum_median 59, p95 74.5: flat and lit from the front

change.to: 0.7, with the frosted acrylic's roughness up so the image blurs into fog and the panel's polished edge catches light

changes.expected: An even, soft glow from inside the panel that lights a little of the concrete reveal around it.

changes.problem: The back-bar's clear acrylic shelves read as a grey veil with no polished, glowing edges.

evidence.measured: lum_median 65, p95 138: an even grey wash; the shelf lines are dim strokes

change.to: edges 1.0; haze 0.008 per m (keep the cones, lift the veil)

changes.expected: Bright, thin edge lines on each shelf, and bottles that show labels and small highlights behind clean acrylic.

changes.problem: Ten identical stools at identical angles and cyan-blue rectangles on the bar make it read as a showroom render and break the one-colour rule.

evidence.measured: small saturated cyan rectangles on a bar top with r 164, g 136, b 122; stools repeat at one angle in [20,300,320,480]

change.from: stools all square to the bar; menus showing a cool tint
change.to: turn the stools 5 to 20 deg at random and pull two out. Make the menus warm paper or kraft. Add a coat on one stool, two half-full rocks glasses and a record out of its sleeve on the bar

changes.expected: The bar reads as occupied minutes ago. No cool hue anywhere except neutral acrylic.

changes.problem: The lounge chairs in the listening room are dead black silhouettes that compete with the speaker.

evidence.measured: lum_median 19.8, chairs near black against a slightly lighter floor

change.to: 3 x 20 W, so the listening room has a low warm fill behind the chairs and the Ember

changes.expected: The chairs read as leather forms with an edge highlight, and the speaker's room has depth.

out_of_scope.request: Make the Ember speaker larger or brighter in its own tint
out_of_scope.why: The speaker's shape, colour and parts are fixed. Its prominence must come from camera, framing and the light around it.

out_of_scope.request: Set the frosted screens flush into the concrete instead of a frame-like surround
out_of_scope.why: The screens' design and mounting are part of the room's fixed design. Only their brightness and frosting roughness may change.

out_of_scope.request: Move the listening-room chairs out of the sightline
out_of_scope.why: The listening room's layout is fixed. The camera change (c1) addresses the sightline instead.
